segments.text:
TYdynges of theſe thinges came vnto the eares of the congregacion, which was in Ieruſalem. And they ſent furth Barnabas, that he ſhould goe vnto Antioche. Whiche when he came, and had ſeen
the grace of God, was glad and exhorted them all, that with purpoſe of heart, they would continually cleaue vnto the Lorde. For he was a good man, and full of the holy goſt and of fayth, and muche people was added vnto the Lorde. Then departed Barnabas to Tharſus, for to ſeke Saul. And when he had found him, he brought him vnto Antioche. And it chaunſed, that a whole yere they hadde theyr conuerſacion with the congregacion there, & taught muche people, inſomuche that the diſciples of Antioche were the firſt that were called Chriſten. In thoſe dayes came Prophetes from the citie of Hieruſalem vnto Antioche. And there ſtode vp one of them, named Agabus, and ſignified by the ſpirite, that there ſhould be greate dearth throughout all the world, which came to paſſe in the Emperoure Cladius dayes. Then the diſciples, euery manne according to his habilitie, purpoſed to ſende ſuccour vnto the brethren which dwelt in Iewry: which thing they alſo dyd, and ſent it to the elders by the handes of Barnabas and Saul.
